_about: Plain words for the Data health screen, per check: title (short), say (what is wrong, for the shop), ask (the owner's question, for decisions), will (what MK changes when the repair runs). The audit files keep the technical detail; build_catalogue.py merges both.

CFG-01.title: Round-off is set to 'Less', so HQ posts every rounded bill's round-off on the wrong side
CFG-01.say: When a bill is rounded (for example 999.60 to 1,000), HQ books the 40 paise on the wrong side of the Round off account. Bill totals and GST are right; only the books are off by twice the round-off.
CFG-01.ask: Change the Round Off charge to 'Add', exactly as HQ's charge screen would? New bills will then be booked correctly, and an old bill re-saved in HQ is corrected too.
CFG-01.will: Changes the Round Off charge from 'Less' to 'Add'. No bill is changed.

CFG-02.title: Bills since 1 Oct 2026 with round-off on the wrong side
CFG-02.say: These bills have the round-off booked on the wrong side (see the Round Off setting above). GST is not affected.
CFG-02.will: Moves each bill's round-off line to the correct side. Amounts, GST, stock and the customer's balance stay the same.

CFG-03.title: Bills before 1 Oct 2026 with round-off on the wrong side
CFG-03.say: The same problem on older bills, from months whose GST returns are probably filed. GST is not affected, only the Round off account.
CFG-03.ask: Correct the round-off side on these older bills too? It changes the books of closed months (by paise per bill), not GST.
CFG-03.will: Moves each older bill's round-off line to the correct side.

CFG-04.title: Bill lines booked to an account that was deleted
CFG-04.say: Some charges (in MK Paints, the round-off on purchase bills) were booked to an account number that no longer exists, so they are missing from every ledger and the trial balance.
CFG-04.ask: Move these lines to the ROUND OFF account?
CFG-04.will: Moves those lines (and the bills' charge rows) to the round-off account.

CFG-05.title: A charge on the bill screen posts to an account that is missing or closed
CFG-05.say: If anyone types an amount in this charge column on a bill, HQ would book it to an account that does not exist.
CFG-05.ask: Choose the account this charge should post to. Only future bills (and bills re-saved in HQ) use it.
CFG-05.will: Sets the charge's account, as HQ's charge screen would.

CFG-06.title: Old unused charges point to missing accounts
CFG-06.say: Charges from earlier years that no bill uses point to accounts that no longer exist. Harmless unless someone puts them back into use.

CFG-07.title: Charge sets left behind by the old MK test version
CFG-07.say: The earlier MK prototype created extra charge sets that no bill type uses. They only clutter HQ's charge-set list.
CFG-07.will: Deletes the unused sets and charges, as HQ's own delete does. Charges that appear on bills are kept.

CFG-08.title: Freight charge set has no name record
CFG-08.say: An old Freight charge set can never load in HQ. Nothing uses it.

CFG-09.title: Bill type is set to round but cannot
CFG-09.say: An unused bill type asks for rounding but has no round-off charge. Only matters if that type is ever used.

CFG-10.title: Sales bills are not rounded to the rupee
CFG-10.say: This sales type bills exact paise (e.g. 1,234.56) while your other sales round to the rupee.
CFG-10.ask: Round this sales type's bills to the rupee, like GST Sales in MK Building Materials? Only future bills change. In MK Paints, set the Round Off charge's account first.
CFG-10.will: Turns on 'Rounded off to 1.00' for this bill type.

CFG-11.title: Bank receipts and payments open with no bank selected
CFG-11.say: The default bank for Bank Receipt / Bank Payment entries is an account that no longer exists, so the operator must pick the bank every time and a wrong pick goes unnoticed.
CFG-11.ask: Which bank should Bank Receipts and Bank Payments open with?
CFG-11.will: Sets that bank as the default on the bank voucher types. No entry already made changes.

CFG-12.title: Old VAT-era account settings on bill types
CFG-12.say: Bill types still carry account settings from the VAT years. HQ no longer reads them.

CFG-13.title: Items without stock-transfer accounts
CFG-13.say: Items created before the Transfer In/Out bill types existed lack those accounts; a stock transfer of such an item would have no account. HQ adds them the next time each item is saved.
CFG-13.will: Adds the missing accounts exactly as HQ would on saving the item. No bill is affected.

CFG-14.title: Item's sales or purchase account does not match its GST rate
CFG-14.say: A wrong rate account files the sale under the wrong GST rate in the summaries.
CFG-14.will: Sets the accounts HQ picks for the item's GST rate. Only future bills use them.

CFG-15.title: Account rows of deleted items
CFG-15.say: HQ leaves these behind when an item is deleted, and never reads them. Left as HQ leaves them.

CFG-16.title: Account rows for bill types that no longer exist

CFG-17.title: Item GST fields do not agree with its GST %
CFG-17.say: An item whose CGST/SGST/IGST fields disagree with its GST % would post tax to the wrong head.
CFG-17.will: Sets the GST fields from the item's GST %, as HQ does on saving the item.

CFG-18.title: GST accounts missing or duplicated for a rate
CFG-18.say: HQ needs a full set of GST accounts for each rate to save items at that rate.
CFG-18.ask: Create the missing GST accounts with HQ's own GST account generation (your accountant).

CFG-19.title: GST input/output accounts are grouped under Income
CFG-19.say: The GST tax and purchase accounts from 2017 sit under Income, so the profit and loss and balance sheet read wrongly. Bills and GST returns are not affected.
CFG-19.ask: Ask your accountant whether to regroup them (tax to Duties & Taxes, purchase heads to Purchase). MK does not change this.

CFG-20.title: Phone Pe / UPI sales can land in Cash
CFG-20.say: No default bank is set for UPI payments, so on some Phone Pe bills the money was received into Cash on hand.

CFG-21.title: GST Sales and IGST Sales price differently
CFG-21.say: GST Sales takes rates including tax, IGST Sales excluding tax, so the same item gives different totals. Probably intended for out-of-state customers.

LED-UNBALANCED.title: Bills whose books do not balance
LED-UNBALANCED.say: On these bills the debit and credit sides differ by more than the round-off. On three, CGST was booked at the full tax and SGST at half.
LED-UNBALANCED.ask: Open each bill in HQ and save it unchanged (F10): HQ books it again from its items. GST lines and filed returns stay as they are.

LED-NO-LEDGER.title: Bills that never reached the books
LED-NO-LEDGER.say: These sales count in GST and stock but are missing from the ledger: sales, output GST and cash are short by the bill amount.
LED-NO-LEDGER.ask: Open each bill in HQ and save it. For CS/826, confirm whether the bill is Rs 900.00 or 900.20.

LED-ORPHAN-ROWS.title: Ledger lines without a bill
LED-ORPHAN-ROWS.say: Ledger lines whose bill was deleted. None found.

LED-HEADER-MISMATCH.title: Ledger lines that disagree with their bill
LED-HEADER-MISMATCH.say: Date, number, party or amount differ between the bill and its ledger lines. None found.

LED-CASH-AS-PARTY.title: Phone Pe and credit sales booked into Cash
LED-CASH-AS-PARTY.say: On these bills Cash on hand was picked as the paying account, although the money went to the bank or is owed by a customer. The cash book is overstated.
LED-CASH-AS-PARTY.ask: For each bill: which account received the money (the bank, Phone Pe, or the customer)? Then open the bill in HQ, set that account, and save.

ADJ-DEAD.title: Old bill-settlement links to entries that no longer exist
ADJ-DEAD.say: Leftovers from previous years. They are invisible in HQ, but in MK Paints some could attach old settlements to new bills when the numbering reaches them.
ADJ-DEAD.will: Removes the links (both of their entries are already gone). No balance or report changes.

ADJ-HALF.title: Payments settled against an opening balance that was later re-created
ADJ-HALF.say: On 8 Jun 2026 HQ's 'update opening balances from last year' re-created the opening entries but left the payments pointing at the old ones. These payments are neither open nor attached, so those parties' bill-wise dues are wrong.
ADJ-HALF.ask: Release these payments so they become on-account, then allocate them again in HQ's bill-wise screen? (Which bills did they really pay?)
ADJ-HALF.will: Releases the payments from the vanished opening entries. Party balances do not change; only the bill-wise allocation does.

ADJ-BAD-LINK.title: Wrong bill-settlement links
ADJ-BAD-LINK.say: A settlement must join a bill and a payment of the same party. None found.

BL-COUNTER.title: Settled amount on an entry does not add up
BL-COUNTER.say: A wrong settled amount shows a paid bill as due (or the reverse).
BL-COUNTER.will: Recomputes the settled amount from the settlement links, as HQ keeps it.

BL-RANGE.title: More settled than billed
BL-RANGE.say: A bill shows more settled against it than its amount. None found.

ADJ-BACKUP-STALE.title: Old entries in HQ's settlement backup list
ADJ-BACKUP-STALE.say: HQ keeps a temporary backup while a bill is edited. These are from previous years, can never match and only clutter the bill-wise screen.
ADJ-BACKUP-STALE.will: Clears the old backup entries (current ones are left alone).

OPEN-MASTER-NOROW.title: Opening balance shown on the account but missing from the books
OPEN-MASTER-NOROW.say: HQ shows these accounts at zero opening, but the account record says otherwise.
OPEN-MASTER-NOROW.ask: Do these accounts really have these opening balances? If yes, enter them in HQ. If not, open the account in HQ and save it.

OPEN-MASTER-DIFF.title: Profit & Loss opening entries
OPEN-MASTER-DIFF.say: HQ's new-year routine leaves two opening entries for last year's profit. HQ is right; nothing to do.

OPEN-DIFF-ACCOUNT.title: Opening Balance Difference account out of step
OPEN-DIFF-ACCOUNT.say: HQ keeps this account equal to the difference of all opening balances. If it drifts, the opening trial balance does not balance.
OPEN-DIFF-ACCOUNT.will: Sets it to the amount HQ computes.

OPEN-TB-DIFFERENCE.title: Opening balances do not balance
OPEN-TB-DIFFERENCE.say: Last year's closing balances do not net to zero; the difference sits in 'Opening Balance Difference'. A question for your accountant.

CASH-NEGATIVE.title: Days with negative cash
CASH-NEGATIVE.say: Cash cannot go below zero. None found.

CASH-BANK-RECON.title: Cash deposits into the bank are not entered
CASH-BANK-RECON.say: Cash in hand keeps growing while the bank looks overdrawn, because no cash-deposit (contra) entry has been made this year.
CASH-BANK-RECON.ask: Are cash deposits and withdrawals entered anywhere? Should they be recorded from now on, and the bank book matched to the statement?

MK-CORE-CHARGE.title: Purchase round-off charge has a machine-made name
MK-CORE-CHARGE.say: The purchase round-off charge was created by the MK test version and has a long code name. It works correctly; you may rename it in HQ to 'Round Off (Purchase)'.

NO-SUPPLIER-PAYMENTS.title: No supplier payments entered this year
NO-SUPPLIER-PAYMENTS.say: MK Paints has credit purchases but no payment entries this year, so every supplier balance only grows.
NO-SUPPLIER-PAYMENTS.ask: Are MK Paints' supplier payments made from another firm's account, or just not entered?

CF01-item-hsn-gst.title: Same product, different HSN or GST rate in the two firms
CF01-item-hsn-gst.say: A product sold by both firms must carry the same HSN code and GST rate. Where they differ, at least one firm reports the wrong HSN or charges the wrong tax.
CF01-item-hsn-gst.ask: For each product, which HSN and rate is right? Then correct the wrong firm's item in Tidy item names or HQ's item screen.

CF02-party-gstin-differs.title: Same party, different GSTIN in the two firms
CF02-party-gstin-differs.say: One of the two GSTINs is wrong (the check digit shows which), so B2B bills under it never reach the party's GSTR-2B.
CF02-party-gstin-differs.ask: Confirm the valid GSTIN, then correct the party in the other firm (Customers & suppliers, or HQ's account screen).

CF03-party-name-spelling.title: Same GSTIN, party name spelled differently in the two firms
CF03-party-name-spelling.say: The same customer or supplier is spelled differently in each firm, which makes matching harder.
CF03-party-name-spelling.ask: Pick one spelling (usually the legal name on the GST portal) and rename the other.

CF04-party-gst-type-state.title: Same GSTIN, different GST type or state in the two firms
CF04-party-gst-type-state.say: One registration cannot be Registered in one firm and Unregistered in the other; it decides whether bills go to B2B or B2C.
CF04-party-gst-type-state.ask: Which is right for each party? Correct the other firm's account.

CF06-transaction-types.title: Bill types set up differently in the two firms
CF06-transaction-types.say: For example, MK Paints GST Sales does not round to the rupee while MK Building Materials does; Opening Stock is tax-inclusive in only one firm.
CF06-transaction-types.ask: Should both firms behave the same? Changes are made in HQ's Transaction Types screen.

CF07-charge-sets.title: Sales bills offer different charges in the two firms
CF07-charge-sets.say: MK Building Materials sales bills offer Freight, Cash Discount and Round Off; MK Paints sales bills only Round Off.
CF07-charge-sets.ask: Should MK Paints sales bills also offer Freight and Cash Discount? (HQ's Charge Sets screen)

CF08-config-flags.title: Safety settings differ between the firms
CF08-config-flags.say: MK Paints does not check for a supplier bill number entered twice, or the same item twice on a bill. One purchase is already entered twice there.
CF08-config-flags.ask: Turn on 'Check duplicate supplier bill no.' and 'Check duplicate item in bill' in MK Paints (HQ's settings screen)?

CF09-company-master.title: Shop details in HQ's company record are wrong
CF09-company-master.say: The PIN code field holds 'PEDDAPURAM' instead of a 6-digit PIN (needed for e-way bills), and MK Paints' mobile number field holds its GSTIN.
CF09-company-master.ask: Give each shop's PIN code and MK Paints' mobile number, and enter them in HQ's Company screen.

GST01-taxed-lines-no-hsn.title: Taxed bill lines without a valid HSN code
GST01-taxed-lines-no-hsn.say: GSTR-1 needs an HSN code on every taxed line; these lines fall out of the HSN summary. Almost all of them are items that still have no HSN.
GST01-taxed-lines-no-hsn.ask: Approve HSN codes for these items (Tidy item names) so the bills can be corrected before the next GSTR-1. Months already filed need an amendment instead.
GST01-taxed-lines-no-hsn.will: Copies the item's HSN onto bill lines whose item now has a valid HSN.

GST02-b2b-invalid-gstin-docs.title: GST bills with a party GSTIN that is not valid
GST02-b2b-invalid-gstin-docs.say: These bills go into GSTR-1 with a GSTIN the portal rejects, so the party cannot claim the tax.
GST02-b2b-invalid-gstin-docs.ask: Find the correct GSTIN (GST portal search) and fix the party; months already filed need an amendment.

GST03-gstin-state-mismatch.title: Party state does not match its GSTIN
GST03-gstin-state-mismatch.say: The state decides CGST+SGST or IGST and the place of supply. HQ sets it from the GSTIN's first two digits; these parties were entered before that.
GST03-gstin-state-mismatch.will: Sets the state from the GSTIN, as HQ does when a GSTIN is typed. No bill changes.

GST04-gstin-but-unregistered.title: Party has a GSTIN but is marked Unregistered
GST04-gstin-but-unregistered.say: Bills to these parties are reported as B2C, so the buyer loses the tax credit.
GST04-gstin-but-unregistered.ask: Are these parties GST-registered? If yes, mark them Registered; if not, remove the GSTIN.

GST05-duplicate-gstin.title: Two party accounts with the same GSTIN
GST05-duplicate-gstin.say: One registration under several accounts splits the party's balance and B2B totals. Sometimes the GSTIN was copied to an unrelated party.
GST05-duplicate-gstin.ask: For each group, which account is the real one? Branches with their own GSTIN are fine.

GST06-party-has-own-gstin.title: A party carries the shop's own GSTIN
GST06-party-has-own-gstin.say: A customer or supplier cannot have your own GSTIN; a bill to it would be a self-invoice.
GST06-party-has-own-gstin.ask: What is this party's real GSTIN? (No bills yet, so only the account needs fixing.)

GST07-itc-without-supplier-gstin.title: GST purchases with tax credit but no supplier GSTIN
GST07-itc-without-supplier-gstin.say: Tax credit can only be claimed against a supplier GSTIN that appears in GSTR-2B. These purchases were booked to Cash on hand or to a supplier without a GSTIN.
GST07-itc-without-supplier-gstin.ask: Who were these suppliers? Cash purchases from GST suppliers should be entered against the supplier's account (paid in cash) so the credit matches. Until then, leave them out of the credit claim.

GST08-invoice-number-gaps.title: Missing sales invoice numbers
GST08-invoice-number-gaps.say: These numbers are missing from the series. Report them as cancelled in GSTR-1 Table 13; do not renumber issued invoices.

GST09-nonstandard-series.title: Bill saved with the wrong series
GST09-nonstandard-series.say: A GST sale was saved as '1/1' instead of a CS number.
GST09-nonstandard-series.ask: Was this a real invoice given to the customer? If so it stays as issued; if not, re-save it in HQ with the next CS number.

GST10-sales-changed-after-gstr1.title: Sales bills changed after their month's GSTR-1 date
GST10-sales-changed-after-gstr1.say: These bills were changed or deleted after the 11th of the next month. If GSTR-1 was already filed, check the filed figures with your accountant.

GST11-duplicate-supplier-bill.title: Same supplier bill entered twice
GST11-duplicate-supplier-bill.say: Probably a purchase entered twice: tax credit and the amount owed are both doubled.
GST11-duplicate-supplier-bill.ask: Are these two separate bills, or one bill entered twice? If twice, delete the extra one in HQ.

GST12-bill-without-tax-summary.title: GST bills missing from the GST registers
GST12-bill-without-tax-summary.say: HQ's GST registers read a tax summary that these bills do not have.
GST12-bill-without-tax-summary.ask: Open each bill in HQ and save it; HQ writes the summary again.

GST13-numbering-out-of-date-order.title: Invoice numbers out of date order
GST13-numbering-out-of-date-order.say: A higher invoice number carries an earlier date than the next one. A common GST audit question; nothing to change.

AU01-prototype-docs-12h-time.title: Bills from the MK test version with 12-hour times
AU01-prototype-docs-12h-time.say: Bills created by the earlier MK prototype store times like '7:16:48 PM', where HQ stores '19:16:48', so time-sorted reports mis-order them.
AU01-prototype-docs-12h-time.will: Converts these times to HQ's 24-hour format. HQ's history copies are left as they are.

AU03-deleted-documents.title: Bills deleted in HQ
AU03-deleted-documents.say: Deleted bills change past returns and stock. Everyone logs in as admin, so HQ cannot say who deleted them.

AU04-users-and-permissions.title: Everyone uses the same HQ login
AU04-users-and-permissions.say: Every bill in both firms is saved under admin, so HQ cannot tell who made or changed a bill. Several test users are never used.
AU04-users-and-permissions.ask: Should each person get their own HQ login? Which unused users (iq, nag, test, T1 and others) can be removed? (HQ's User screen)

SEC01-weak-plaintext-passwords.title: HQ passwords are weak
SEC01-weak-plaintext-passwords.say: Most HQ users, admin included, have their user name as the password, and HQ stores passwords unprotected. The passwords are not shown here.
SEC01-weak-plaintext-passwords.ask: Change the admin password and remove the test users in HQ's user screen.

SEC02-plaintext-db-credentials.title: Database administrator password is stored in HQ tables
SEC02-plaintext-db-credentials.say: Anyone who can read one HQ table gets full control of all databases.
SEC02-plaintext-db-credentials.ask: Have the SQL Server administrator (sa) password changed to a strong one. Test on a copy first that HQ still starts.

SEC03-gsp-credentials.title: GST e-filing passwords are stored in the databases
SEC03-gsp-credentials.say: Ask HQ support whether these are the shop's or the vendor's, and keep database backups safe.

HL03-orphan-rows-template.title: Leftover rows from HQ's demo company
HL03-orphan-rows-template.say: Rows from HQ's template company that nothing reads. Left as HQ leaves them.

HL05-party-without-address.title: Old parties without an address record
HL05-party-without-address.say: Parties imported from earlier years (names ending -2018, -2019...) have no address record, so some reports skip them. Saving the account in HQ adds it, or they can be made inactive.

HL07-hsn-master-junk.title: HQ's demo 'Mobiles' HSN codes in use
HL07-hsn-master-junk.say: MK Paints' HSN list still has HQ's demo 'Mobiles' codes, and four items picked them, so their bills report a mobile-phone HSN.
HL07-hsn-master-junk.ask: What HSN should these items have? (Putty is usually 3214.) Once they are corrected, MK can remove the demo codes.
HL07-hsn-master-junk.will: Removes the demo codes from the HSN list (only when no item uses them any more).

TX01_HALF_SAVED_BILL.title: Bills that were never finished in HQ
TX01_HALF_SAVED_BILL.say: HQ saves a bill's lines as they are typed and the accounts only on F10. These bills were interrupted: the goods count as sold, but the money never reached the cash book or the GST ledgers.
TX01_HALF_SAVED_BILL.ask: Did these sales really happen? If yes, re-save each bill in HQ (or through MK) so its accounts are written; if not, delete it. For CS/826, is the bill Rs 900.00 or 900.20?

TX02_HALF_SAVED_ORDER.title: Estimates and orders that were never finished
TX02_HALF_SAVED_ORDER.say: These estimates were interrupted before F10, so their charge and tax-summary rows are missing. Orders do not touch accounts or stock.
TX02_HALF_SAVED_ORDER.will: Adds the missing rows with HQ's own procedures, as a finished order carries them. Accounts and stock are not affected.

TX03_LINES_CHANGED_AFTER_SAVE.title: Bill lines changed after the bill was saved
TX03_LINES_CHANGED_AFTER_SAVE.say: On these bills a rate or quantity was changed after saving, but the bill total and the accounts kept the old figure, so the printed bill, GST and the books disagree.
TX03_LINES_CHANGED_AFTER_SAVE.ask: Which is right: the saved total (put the lines back as last saved), or the new lines (re-save the bill with a new total)? For the five purchases the difference is paise.

TX04_DUPLICATE_LINE_NO_OPEN.title: Two lines with the same line number (orders and recent bills)
TX04_DUPLICATE_LINE_NO_OPEN.say: Lines inserted in the middle of a bill took their neighbour's number. Totals are right; only the print order is unstable.
TX04_DUPLICATE_LINE_NO_OPEN.will: Numbers the lines 1, 2, 3… in their current order. Nothing else changes.

TX05_DUPLICATE_LINE_NO_POSTED.title: Two lines with the same line number (bills before 1 Oct 2026)
TX05_DUPLICATE_LINE_NO_POSTED.say: The same, on bills of months whose GST is filed. Amounts are right.
TX05_DUPLICATE_LINE_NO_POSTED.ask: May MK renumber these bills' lines 1, 2, 3…? Nothing else on the bills changes.
TX05_DUPLICATE_LINE_NO_POSTED.will: Numbers the lines 1, 2, 3… in their current order.

TX06_ORDER_SUPPLIED_TWICE.title: An estimate billed twice, or billed to another party
TX06_ORDER_SUPPLIED_TWICE.say: The same estimate lines were turned into two sale bills (e.g. SO/135 into CS/314 and CS/315), or into a bill for a different customer. One of the two may be a duplicate bill.
TX06_ORDER_SUPPLIED_TWICE.ask: Are both bills of each pair genuine, separate sales?

TX07_STOCK_DRIFT.title: Item stock figure out of date
TX07_STOCK_DRIFT.say: HQ does not refresh an item's stock after a bill is deleted, a line is removed while editing, or opening stock is redone, so the stock shown is stale.
TX07_STOCK_DRIFT.will: Runs HQ's own 'Update ClosingStock to Items List'. No bill changes.

TX08_NEGATIVE_STOCK.title: Items with negative stock
TX08_NEGATIVE_STOCK.say: More was sold than received in this year's books, mostly because last year's negative stock was carried into this year's opening stock.
TX08_NEGATIVE_STOCK.ask: Do you want stock tracked for these items? If yes, a physical count is needed; if not, the negative opening lines can be set to zero (next line).

TX09_NEGATIVE_OPENING_STOCK.title: Opening stock with negative quantities
TX09_NEGATIVE_OPENING_STOCK.say: HQ's new-year tool copied last year's negative stock into this year's opening stock. A negative opening is impossible on the shelf.
TX09_NEGATIVE_OPENING_STOCK.ask: Set these negative opening quantities to zero? Opening stock value does not change (these lines have rate 0), but every such item's stock goes up.
TX09_NEGATIVE_OPENING_STOCK.will: Sets the negative opening quantities to zero and refreshes those items' stock with HQ's procedure.

TX10_OPENING_STOCK_IRREGULAR.title: Opening stock entered twice or on the wrong date

TX11_BILL_TIME_12H.title: Bills from the MK test version with 12-hour times
TX11_BILL_TIME_12H.say: Bills written by the earlier MK prototype store the time like '7:16:48 PM' instead of HQ's '19:16:48', so time-sorted reports mis-order them.
TX11_BILL_TIME_12H.will: Writes the same time in HQ's 24-hour format. Nothing else changes.

TX12_RENUMBERED_BILL.title: Bill numbers changed after saving
TX12_RENUMBERED_BILL.say: These bills were renumbered after saving: CS/665 became '1/1' (a hole in the series), and a bill reuses the number CS/326.
TX12_RENUMBERED_BILL.ask: Which number did the customer get, and which number went into GSTR-1? MK corrects the number only on your answer.

TX14_SUPPLIER_DATE_DEFAULTED.title: Supplier invoice date never entered on purchases
TX14_SUPPLIER_DATE_DEFAULTED.say: HQ kept the day the purchase was typed as the supplier's invoice date. GSTR-2B matching uses the real invoice date, so these purchases will not match.
TX14_SUPPLIER_DATE_DEFAULTED.ask: Should the purchase date be used as the supplier invoice date, or will you give the real dates from the supplier bills?

TX15_DUE_BEFORE_BILL_DATE.title: Due date before the bill date
TX15_DUE_BEFORE_BILL_DATE.say: Bills typed days later kept an old due date. They are cash bills, so nothing is affected; check the due date when back-dating.

TX16_ZERO_RATE_SALE_LINE.title: Items given at rate 0
TX16_ZERO_RATE_SALE_LINE.say: These sale lines took stock out with no charge. Fine for free samples; otherwise a missed charge.

TX17_ORPHAN_PAYMENT_SPLIT.title: Payment split left from an abandoned bill
TX17_ORPHAN_PAYMENT_SPLIT.say: The 'Others' payment screen saved a split before the bill was abandoned. It is empty and nothing can reach it.
TX17_ORPHAN_PAYMENT_SPLIT.will: Removes the empty split, as HQ's delete would have.

TX18_PRIOR_YEAR_LEFTOVERS.title: Last year's payment splits
TX18_PRIOR_YEAR_LEFTOVERS.say: Copied over by HQ's new-year routine; nothing reads them. Left as HQ leaves them.

TX20_ORPHAN_DOCUMENT_ROWS.title: Bill rows without a bill
TX20_ORPHAN_DOCUMENT_ROWS.say: Lines or account rows left by an interrupted delete.
TX20_ORPHAN_DOCUMENT_ROWS.will: Removes them as HQ's delete does (rows with settlements are kept for you).

TX21_LINE_GST_ARITHMETIC.title: Line GST does not add up
TX21_LINE_GST_ARITHMETIC.say: Tax that is not taxable value × rate would file wrong GST. None found.

TX22_LINE_ITEM_REFERENCES.title: Bill lines with a missing item

P-DUP-NAME.title: Same customer or supplier entered more than once
P-DUP-NAME.say: These accounts look like the same party under slightly different names (e.g. 'Y K CONSTRUCTIONS' and 'YK CONSTRUCTIONS', or an old '-2018-2019-2020' copy). HQ only catches exact duplicates.
P-DUP-NAME.ask: For each group: the same party, or different ones? HQ has no merge; a duplicate with no bills can be switched off, and one with bills needs its balance moved by a transfer entry.

P-DUP-GSTIN.title: One GSTIN on two party accounts
P-DUP-GSTIN.say: A GSTIN belongs to one business. Two accounts with it split the party's balance, or one of them carries someone else's GSTIN.
P-DUP-GSTIN.ask: Same business? If not, which account has the wrong GSTIN?

P-SAME-PAN.title: Different GSTINs with the same PAN
P-SAME-PAN.say: Either the same business registered twice (allowed) or one GSTIN is a mistyped copy of the other.

P-DUP-MOBILE.title: Same mobile number on different parties
P-DUP-MOBILE.say: Either related parties, or the same customer entered twice.

P-SPLIT-BALANCE.title: One party's balance split over several accounts
P-SPLIT-BALANCE.say: For example DEVI SEA FOODS (two units) or UPRIGHT projects (115,707 Dr on one account, 97,783 Cr on the other): the real dues are hidden.
P-SPLIT-BALANCE.ask: Are they the same party? If so, should the balances be combined by a transfer entry today (old bills stay as they are)?

P-NAME-PLACEHOLDER.title: Accounts named by a phone number or one or two letters
P-NAME-PLACEHOLDER.say: An account called '9030688374' or 'Vd' cannot be found by name and is usually a second account for a known customer.

P-GST-FORMAT.title: GSTIN stored with spaces or small letters
P-GST-FORMAT.say: A space inside the GSTIN makes portal uploads and searches fail, although the number is right.
P-GST-FORMAT.will: Re-saves the account as HQ's account screen does, with the GSTIN in capitals and without spaces.

P-GST-LENGTH.title: GSTIN is not 15 characters
P-GST-LENGTH.say: Not a valid GSTIN at all. GST returns reject it, and HQ will not let anyone save the account until it is corrected.
P-GST-LENGTH.ask: What is the correct GSTIN? (From the party's bill or the GST portal.) If the party is no longer used, the GSTIN can be cleared.

P-GST-CHECKDIGIT.title: GSTIN mistyped (fails the check digit)
P-GST-CHECKDIGIT.say: The last character of a GSTIN is a check. These fail it, mostly an O typed for 0 or I for 1. The portal rejects bills with them.
P-GST-CHECKDIGIT.ask: Where MK found the one-letter correction that makes it valid, confirm it for this party (check the party's bill if unsure).
P-GST-CHECKDIGIT.will: Re-saves the account with the corrected GSTIN, as HQ's account screen does.

P-GST-TYPE.title: Party has a valid GSTIN but is marked Unregistered
P-GST-TYPE.say: Bills to it are reported as unregistered (B2C), so the party loses the tax credit. HQ will not save the account in this state.
P-GST-TYPE.will: Re-saves the account as Registered, with the state from the GSTIN, as HQ's account screen does.

P-GST-STATE.title: Party state does not match its GSTIN
P-GST-STATE.say: The state decides CGST+SGST or IGST. A Telangana GSTIN saved with Andhra Pradesh is filed as a local sale.
P-GST-STATE.will: Re-saves the account with the state from the GSTIN, as HQ does when a GSTIN is typed.

P-STATE-CAPTION.title: Party state blank or in an old spelling
P-STATE-CAPTION.say: HQ shows a blank state as Andhra Pradesh, but stores nothing; '36-Telengana' is an old spelling not in HQ's list.
P-STATE-CAPTION.will: Re-saves the account with the state HQ itself shows (or the current spelling).

P-GST-PAN.title: PAN does not match the GSTIN

P-CASH-KNOWN-PARTY.title: Cash bills typed with a known party's name
P-CASH-KNOWN-PARTY.say: The bill was made to Cash with the party's name typed in, so it is missing from that party's account and history.
P-CASH-KNOWN-PARTY.ask: Should such bills be made on the party's own account? Past bills are changed only on your word.

P-CASH-GSTIN-UNREG.title: Purchase bills from registered suppliers saved as unregistered
P-CASH-GSTIN-UNREG.say: The bill carries the supplier's GSTIN but was saved as unregistered, so the input credit does not show in HQ's GST reports.
P-CASH-GSTIN-UNREG.ask: Re-save these bills in HQ as registered so the input credit appears?

P-CASH-GSTIN-NO-ACCOUNT.title: GST bills for a GSTIN with no party account
P-CASH-GSTIN-NO-ACCOUNT.say: Cash bills with a supplier GSTIN that no account carries.
P-CASH-GSTIN-NO-ACCOUNT.ask: Create an account for the supplier if you buy from it again.

P-CASH-GSTIN-STALE.title: Old GSTIN kept on earlier cash bills
P-CASH-GSTIN-STALE.say: The account's GSTIN was corrected later; cash bills keep the old one. Mostly estimates, which are not reported.

P-CASH-MODE-PARTY.title: Parties billed as Cash by default
P-CASH-MODE-PARTY.say: Bills to these parties go to Cash on hand, so their account and dues never show those sales.
P-CASH-MODE-PARTY.ask: Should this party be billed on credit by default (bills then appear in its account), or stay cash? Only future bills change.
P-CASH-MODE-PARTY.will: Re-saves the account with bill mode Credit, as HQ's account screen does.

P-PLACEHOLDER.title: The '=' walk-in account carries a balance
P-PLACEHOLDER.say: '=' only holds the name on walk-in estimates, but it carries 69,827 from last year and credit note CRE/1.
P-PLACEHOLDER.ask: Who owes this amount: write it off, or move it to named customers? Was CRE/1 meant for K B K BIOTECH?

P-NO-ADDRESS.title: Parties without an address record
P-NO-ADDRESS.say: Parties imported in Dec 2023 have no address record, so they have no GST type, GSTIN or state, and reports show blanks.
P-NO-ADDRESS.will: Re-saves each account as HQ's account screen does when it is opened and saved unchanged (blank address, Unregistered, Andhra Pradesh).

P-NOT-FORM-SAVED.title: Parties never saved in HQ's account screen
P-NOT-FORM-SAVED.say: Imported accounts lack some rows HQ's account screen writes. Harmless; HQ adds them when the account is next saved.

P-OPEN-MASTER.title: Opening balance on the account differs from the books
P-OPEN-MASTER.say: HQ's ledgers use one opening figure and the account record holds another; the next save in HQ silently overwrites the account record.
P-OPEN-MASTER.ask: Which figure is right? The books (MK re-saves the account) or the account record (enter it as the opening in HQ)?
P-OPEN-MASTER.will: Re-saves the account as HQ does, keeping the books' opening figure.

P-DUP-CODE.title: Two accounts with the same code (HQ cannot save either)
P-DUP-CODE.say: Old '-2018-2019-2020' copies got the same shortened code as another account, so HQ refuses to save both.
P-DUP-CODE.will: Gives the newer account of each pair a new code by HQ's own rule (A + 1000 + account no.), re-saving it as HQ does.

P-GROUP-TYPE.title: Customers and suppliers in the wrong group
P-GROUP-TYPE.say: Customers filed under Fixed Assets or Computers (SIGMA SEA FOODS alone 1.42 lakh) inflate fixed assets and are missing from Sundry Debtors in the balance sheet.
P-GROUP-TYPE.ask: Move all of them to Sundry Debtors / Sundry Creditors, as HQ's account screen does for these types? Bills do not change; balance sheets printed earlier will read differently.
P-GROUP-TYPE.will: Re-saves each account under Sundry Debtors (customers) or Sundry Creditors (suppliers).

P-TREE.title: Party misplaced in the chart of accounts
P-TREE.will: Re-saves the account into its group.

P-DORMANT.title: Unused parties cluttering the lists
P-DORMANT.say: Accounts carried forward since 2023 with no bill, no balance and no use. They clutter every party list and invite duplicates.
P-DORMANT.ask: Switch these accounts off? They stay in HQ and can be switched on again at any time.
P-DORMANT.will: Re-saves each account with 'Active' unticked, as HQ's account screen does.

P-ORPHAN-REFS.title: Rows pointing at deleted accounts
P-ORPHAN-REFS.say: Contact rows and other leftovers of deleted accounts (in MK Paints, the round-off rows; see 'Bill lines booked to an account that was deleted').

P-BALANCE-SIDE.title: Customer in credit, or supplier in debit
P-BALANCE-SIDE.say: Allowed (an advance or overpayment), but often a receipt booked to the wrong one of two duplicate accounts.
